A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LAPA research. Their full text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original Language Table, SIMPLER, single-arm and bimanual robot experiments, alongside scaling and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original simulation and single-arm robot results and reports additional comparisons and ablations in its appendices.

M1.justification: The quantization, latent-action pretraining, and action-finetuning pipeline remains unchanged, including NSVQ, cross-attention, the LWM backbone, and action-head replacement. V2 supplies embedding-difference, CNN, and stop-gradient details without establishing that the underlying procedure changed.

E1.justification: V2 removes the entire 14-DoF bimanual evaluation described in v1 Section 4.5, Appendix B, and Table 17, eliminating a distinct embodiment and coordinated manipulation scenario. Language Table, SIMPLER, the three single-arm tasks, and the pretraining datasets remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds OpenVLA to the SIMPLER comparison in Table 11, alongside the retained Scratch, UniPi, VPT, LAPA, and ActionVLA results. OpenVLA's earlier participation in real-world experiments does not make this additional comparator participation unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds controlled evaluations varying frame windows, fine-tuning data quantity, and human pretraining data at 10% versus full scale. Table 3 also changes the reported human pretraining count from 220k to 200k, while Section 4.5 still describes 220k videos; the actual subset or any rerun is not established. Retained benchmark rollout counts and scoring rules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds three substantive analyses: temporal-window sensitivity, fine-tuning sample efficiency against Scratch, and human-video pretraining data scaling. These extend the earlier model/data/token-capacity ablations. Existing latent-action visualizations, task-distribution analysis, pairwise win rates, and UniPi failure cases are retained despite relocation.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly identifies the existing uncertainty values in the Language Table summary and main performance figures as standard errors. Conversely, v1's Bridgev2-SIMPLER summary plot with error bars disappears, while its retained detailed table provides point estimates only. Neither PDF establishes additional training seeds or repeated runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds OpenVLA's SIMPLER results, including 36.4% average success, the 10%-human-data LAPA results, and Figure 15's ablation curves. It removes bimanual results of 30.21% for LAPA and 26.04% for OpenVLA. Tables 13–16 correct swapped Bridge LAPA/ActionVLA labels: Table 16 now assigns 36.83% to LAPA and 32.61% to ActionVLA, agreeing with the retained headline results rather than demonstrating a performance gain.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix A adds explicit mathematical specification, including the embedding difference d1 = e2 - e1 and quantization, noise-substitution, decoding, and reconstruction expressions in Equations 1–4. V1 provides a schematic and verbal account. No theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract strengthens novelty from an unsupervised VLA pretraining method to the first such method. The principal claims about action-label-free pretraining, human-video transfer, the 6.22-point OpenVLA advantage, and over 30-fold pretraining efficiency remain.

C2.justification: V2 attributes large-window failures to limited quantizer capacity and OpenVLA's SIMPLER weakness to real-to-sim transfer. It removes the bimanual low-performance discussion and the earlier latent-size saturation qualification. Appendix F interprets human-data scaling positively, although Table 12 shows mixed individual-task effects.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands the quantizer specification with CNN-controlled sequence length, gradient stopping, and the reconstruction loss. It newly documents shared data between pretraining stages and frame intervals of 0.6 seconds for robot videos and 2.4 seconds for human videos, including default Bridgev2 H = 3. The abstract also changes the code/checkpoint release statement from present to future tense; actual availability is unresolved.

R1.justification: V2 adds He et al. (2024) on actionable discrete diffusion policies and removes Damen et al. (2022) with the bimanual discussion. It strengthens the novelty claim and condenses distinctions between prior video-learning approaches, while retaining the main research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: Bridgev2-SIMPLER results move to the appendix, generalization results move into the main text, and latent-action analysis and additional ablations receive separate appendices. Related work and several introductory passages are condensed, while the method explanation expands and LAPA terminology is clarified.

P2.justification: Figures and tables are extensively redistributed between the main text and appendices. V2 redraws the quantizer diagram, adds the two-panel ablation Figure 15, expands SIMPLER tables, and removes the bimanual table and standalone Bridgev2-SIMPLER plot. It also corrects table labels and revises figure captions and axes.

improvement.justification: Expanded quantizer documentation, additional sensitivity and data-efficiency experiments, and corrected Bridge model attribution improve reproducibility and the consistency of the evidence. These gains are limited by the loss of the distinct bimanual evaluation, unexplained human-video count differences, and overbroad interpretation of some scaling results. The net improvement is modest.
